title: Matanucke (Staten Island)
summary: This Staten Island entry gathers related names discussed in Tooker, including Matanucke, Monocknong, and Aquehonga Manacknong. Monocknong is treated here as a cross-reference variant, not as a separate mapped site.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Staten Island coordinate from LatLong.net; not an exact historical deed coordinate.
history_content: The Staten Island name-family context together remain grouped here instead of splitting closely related island-name variants into separate entries.
translation_content:
Related forms include Matanucke, Monocknong, Aquehonga Manacknong, and Manacknong. Tooker rejects the romanticized "Haunted Woods" explanation for Monocknong and points back to Aquehonga Manacknong, interpreted as a place at the foot of a high bank.

Why Place Names Matter

“As linguistic artifacts, place names tell us something not only about the structure and content of the physical environment itself but also provide valuable insights into the ways humans experience the world.”

— Thomas F. Thornton, Anthropological Studies of Native American Place Naming (1997), quoted by JSTOR Daily with original journal citation
whereintheworld_content: The blue marker uses Staten Island as a broad reference point for related island names in the surrounding region.
